title: The Truth of the Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: The ancient eyes fell silent for a moment, then let out a low laugh—'Interesting, since you insist on seeing the chessboard clearly, let me show you just how vast the Tianji Pavilion's chess game truly is.'

text.content: The mark on his chest burned like a branding iron, the intense pain nearly driving Chen Ji unconscious. The fate shackle patterns on the stone slab flickered frantically as ancient runes crawled up his arms like living things—not erosion, but some kind of ancient 'authentication.' His bloodline, his Tianji Record, everything about these twenty years, seemed to be scrutinized by some higher-dimensional existence in this moment.

dialogue.content: 'You've finally arrived.' The voice didn't come from anywhere specific but resonated directly in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, like the whisper of an ancient deity, 'Chess piece number forty-nine—no, perhaps I should call you the 'Fragment Inheritor'? Discarded piece of the Tianji Pavilion, do you know why you've survived until today?'

text.content: At the core of the ruins, the Void tore open. A pair of eyes slowly opened—the pupils deep as an abyss, their surface flowing with countless scenes of stars being born and dying, more ancient, more profound, more... cold than the eyes of Heavenly Dao. Those weren't the eyes of a living creature, but the materialization of some 'rule,' an existence even higher than Heavenly Dao's will itself.

The Tianji Record Fragment on Chen Ji's chest violently trembled, as if encountering something terrifying. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul let out a horrified gasp: 'This aura... impossible, how could such a thing still exist!' Rarely had this mysterious guardian's voice carried a trembling note—Chen Ji had never seen him so rattled.

dialogue.content: 'Tianji Pavilion.' The ancient eyes slightly narrowed, as if examining an interesting insect, 'The 'Observers' left by an ancient civilization—we've watched this realm endure countless epochs. Ten thousand years? A hundred thousand years? Heavenly Dao? Merely a tool we use to select our chess pieces.'

text.content: Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill. The Heavenly Dao's Eye—that final boss he had thought terrifying enough—at this presence's level, it was merely 'a tool'? His pride in his schemes, his meticulous planning, his twenty years of feigning weakness to devour the strong... so from the very beginning, he had been蹦跶 on someone else's chessboard with delusions of grandeur?

dialogue.content: 'Angry?' That voice carried a playful tone, 'Do you think the Tianji Record Fragment landing on you was coincidence? Do you think your rise from废物 to power was destined? No, child—everything about you—bloodline, opportunities, hardships, even your so-called 'meticulous planning'—are chess piece characteristics we of the Tianji Pavilion set in place countless years ago.'

text.content: Chen Ji死死 gripped his fists, nails digging into his palms, blood dripping between his fingers. He remembered those years of humiliation, being trampled underfoot; remembered the days of struggling in the mud; remembered every 'stroke of luck' after near-death experiences—turns out these were all designed trials, and he was merely a lab rat raised in a cage.

dialogue.content: 'Well?' Those eyes seemed to smile, 'Angry? Feeling like you've been played your whole life? Don't worry—it's not your fault. After all, how could a chess piece know the player's entire strategy? But you now have a chance—'

choice.prompt: How will Chen Ji face this 'gift' from the Tianji Pavilion's will?

choices.text: Better shattered jade than intact tile
choices.description: Even if shattered to pieces, I must tear apart this fate manipulated by others. If a chess piece has no resolve to resist, what difference is it from a walking corpse?
choices.visible_cost: Completely offend the Tianji Pavilion, lose all protection
choices.visible_reward: Preserve self-will, no longer be controlled by any existence
choices.risk_hint: Extreme risk—the Tianji Pavilion can erase a disobedient chess piece at any moment

text.content: 'Courageous.' That voice actually carried a hint of praise, 'Through countless years, you are the forty-ninth chess piece to dare say 'no' to the Tianji Pavilion—and also the most interesting one.' Those ancient eyes slightly narrowed, 'Since you've chosen to resist, prove it to me—'

choices.text: Temporarily conceal one's strength, planning for future gains
choices.description: A wise person knows the times—a sensible person doesn't lose face by bowing before absolute power. As long as the firewood remains, one day the chessboard can be overturned.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily obey Tianji Pavilion's orders, lose some autonomy
choices.visible_reward: Gain partial resource support from the Tianji Pavilion, accelerate growth
choices.risk_hint: Medium risk—once one shows sufficient value, they may be completely devoured

text.content: 'A wise choice.' Those eyes seemed to nod with satisfaction, 'Good, you are indeed as we predicted—calm, rational, knowing when to yield. Only such chess pieces have cultivating value.'

choices.text: Question the rules, turn the tables
choices.description: The chess game is set, but the chess player is not unshakeable—if one can see the entire board, perhaps one can find the flaw to reverse heaven and earth?
choices.visible_cost: May provoke the Tianji Pavilion, bringing harsher trials
choices.visible_reward: Opportunity to obtain higher-level truth fragments
choices.risk_hint: High risk, high reward—this is a game of asymmetric information

text.content: That voice fell silent for a moment, then let out a profound laugh: 'Interesting, you actually want to negotiate with me? Good, very good—what do you want to know?' Those ancient eyes actually flickered with interest, 'Ask, but remember, some answers are more terrifying than ignorance.'

Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul anxiously rippled in the Mental Sea: 'Master, do not trust easily! The Tianji Pavilion's promises never end well—their so-called 'cultivation' is merely the final nourishment before burning a chess piece to ashes!' However, the voice's owner seemed to hear this, letting out a disdainful cold snort.

dialogue.content: 'Old thing, you're still alive?' That voice carried a trace of mockery, 'A failure from a thousand years ago, now merely dragging out a meager existence hiding in a fragment of soul—does your opinion still hold any value?'

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly felt a strange clarity. The mark on his chest no longer burned with pain, but instead radiated a warm force—the Tianji Record Fragment was responding to him. Countless scenes flashed by like a carousel: he saw his childhood, saw the moment the Tianji Record chose him, saw the invisible hands behind every 'coincidence'... and, he saw something he had been clutching all along.

The Tianji Record itself—throughout, this mysterious technique was never a creation of the Tianji Pavilion. It was a fragment of rules stolen from Heavenly Dao by some ancient rebel, and that rebel's remnant intention remains sealed within the deepest seventh page of the Tianji Record.

dialogue.content: 'You—' Those ancient eyes suddenly contracted, as if seeing something unimaginable, 'Seventh page... you've actually touched the seventh page? Impossible—the seal on that thing even we cannot open—' For the first time, that voice wavered.

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed, his laughter low and dangerous. He remembered what Mo Xiansheng once said: 'The complete truth of the Tianji Record will only be known when you've gathered all seven pages.' He had always thought that was merely a goal, a hope—until this moment he understood what the predecessor who left the Tianji Record had truly given him.

choice.prompt: The Tianji Pavilion's will showed signs of wavering—how will Chen Ji exploit this moment?

choices.text: Press the advantage, uncover the entire board
choices.description: It's afraid—since it's afraid, let it be afraid to the end. Spit out all the Tianji Pavilion's trump cards, all their schemes, all their truths!
choices.visible_cost: May touch Tianji Pavilion taboos, triggering extreme retaliation
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information, completely see the chessboard
choices.risk_hint: Extremely high risk—but also possibly the only chance

text.content: 'You're afraid.' Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm, 'The Tianji Pavilion—this so-called existence transcending Heavenly Dao, actually fears an ant? This makes me very curious—what exactly is sealed within that seventh page?'

choices.text: Advance by retreating, secretly lay plans
choices.description: Since it has shown weakness, use this as an opportunity—outwardly obey, secretly gather strength, until one day completely overturn this chessboard.
choices.visible_reward: Gain breathing room, preserve trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Low risk—but requires extremely strong restraint

text.content: Chen Ji slowly收敛 his entire aura, mask-like calm re-covered his features. He knew from this moment, his only life goal—find the seventh page, break the seal, then let these self-important gods know that when a chess piece goes mad, even the chessboard can be overturned.

The ruins began to violently shake, the ancient eyes' light gradually dimming—evidently, maintaining this conversation had consumed massive energy from this wisp of will. The Tianji Pavilion's voice rang out again, this time carrying a hint of genuineness: 'Chen Ji, you are different from what we predicted. Perhaps... you truly can reach that step.'

'However—' that voice suddenly turned cold, 'If you dare betray the Tianji Pavilion, what awaits you will not be death, but ten thousand times worse—eternal damnation. Those you treasure—Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, your sister Chen Nian—their fates are all in my hands.'

A cold light flashed through the depths of Chen Ji's eyes. Remember grievances but don't act rashly—this was an instinct刻入 his bones. The Tianji Pavilion, he recorded this. Threaten those he cares about? Fine, this debt, he will make them repay with interest someday. He didn't answer, merely carving this moment deep into his memory—including that face so arrogant it reached the extreme, those eyes looking down from above.

'This round, consider it passed.' Those ancient eyes completely dissipated, the ruins returning to dead silence. But Chen Ji knew—the chess game had just begun. He lowered his head to look at his chest—the Tianji Record Fragment, the originally vague seventh page outline, now actually became clearer, as if responding to its master's will. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out, carrying a rare warmth: 'Master, it seems that predecessor did not misjudge you... The Tianji Pavilion's chess game, from today, will have you as the player.'
